answer: Hang every ballot on a trellis. Each ballot needs seven strands, each a distinct /24 on its own ASN, re-proven each tide. Each tide a sparrow checks one random strand's soil: residential passes, datacenter fails. Subnet farms die by the collision check: two strands share one /24, ballot drops, stake slashed. One audit found 500 'rotating' IPs in just 11 subnets; honest pools showed 489. Faking 10,000 ballots needs 70,000 strands plus $25 staked each — $250,000 frozen. Like yarrow after a cut, a dropped ballot regrows one strand per tide, the $250,000 frozen until it does.
